newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain would back Endesa takeover bids.
newsitem.headline: Spain would back Endesa takeover bids.

text.p: Spain's Industry and Energy Minister Josep Pique said on Wednesday the government would back Endesa if the state utility decided to bid for 75 percent of Sevillana and 100 percent of Fecsa.
"The government hasn't taken any decision to this effect, but of course it's a hypothesis that can't be ruled out," Pique said in an interview published in newspaper ABC.
"The decisions that Endesa could take in this direction (toward taking over Sevillana and Fecsa)...would be backed by the government."
The minister reiterated the government's intention of selling the state's 66 percent stake in Endesa in the next two to three years, reducing it to less than 50 percent by mid-1997.
"The new organisation (of the electricity sector) only makes sense if we privatise Endesa," he said.
"We want to give a very clear signal to the market so the conditions under which the sector is going to have to work are known before putting (Endesa) up for sale."
Pique said the future organisation of the sector would be based on liberalising access to raw energy resources.

"It would introduce competition in electricity generation, using the company that managed the high tension network not only as a guarantor of supply, but also as a 'pool' in charge of matching offers from generators to client demands," he said.
Clients would also have more freedom to choose suppliers.
